text: {"criteria":{"task":{"band":5.5,"summary":"The essay addresses both sides of the question and gives a clear, if somewhat hedged, position ('I am agree with this opinion in some way but not all'), and it reaches the 250-word minimum. Main ideas (public transport helps people without cars; new roads ease congestion) are relevant but developed only through simple, sometimes personal examples, and the reasoning stays general. The conclusion restates the position adequately, so TR sits at 5.5 rather than 6.0.","strengths":[{"quote":"I am agree with this opinion in some way but not all.","comment":"A position is stated early and is recognisable, which satisfies the requirement for a clear stance."},{"quote":"In conclusion, I think goverment should spend more money for public transport but also build some road when it is necessary.","comment":"The conclusion restates the balanced position and links back to both sides of the question."}],"issues":[{"quote":"For example my father drive to work everyday and he spend two hour in the road.","comment":"The supporting example is personal and thin; it does not extend the argument about road building at a general level.","suggestion":"Broaden the example: 'For instance, in fast-growing cities such as Beijing, commuters can spend two hours a day in traffic because road capacity has not kept pace with car ownership.'"},{"quote":"Also if more people take bus, the city will be more quiet and the air will be more clean","comment":"The environmental point is asserted rather than explained, so the idea is not fully extended.","suggestion":"Add a causal chain: 'Because one bus can replace around forty cars, shifting commuters to public transport would cut both congestion and exhaust emissions.'"}]},"coherence":{"band":5.0,"summary":"Ideas are arranged in paragraphs with a broadly logical progression from public transport to roads to a balanced conclusion. However, cohesion is mechanical, relying on 'Firstly/Secondly/Also/But', and several sentences begin with 'Because', which weakens flow. Referencing is basic and sometimes unclear, so the essay does not yet reach 6.0.","strengths":[{"quote":"Firstly, public transport is good for people.","comment":"Paragraphs are signposted, giving the reader a clear structure to follow."},{"quote":"But I think public transport is more important than road.","comment":"A contrast is used to signal the writer's overall preference before the conclusion."}],"issues":[{"quote":"Because many people dont have car and they need bus and train to go work and school.","comment":"Starting a sentence with 'Because' as a fragment disrupts the flow and is a common cohesion error.","suggestion":"Combine with the previous sentence: 'This is because many people do not own a car and rely on buses and trains to get to work or school.'"},{"quote":"Also the train is too expensive for student. So goverment should make it cheap and more fast.","comment":"Short sentences joined by 'Also/So' create a choppy, mechanical rhythm.","suggestion":"Link ideas with a subordinator: 'Since trains are also too expensive for students, the government should make fares cheaper and services faster.'"}]},"lexical":{"band":5.0,"summary":"Vocabulary is adequate for the topic but limited, with frequent repetition of basic items ('good', 'bad', 'important', 'more'). There are noticeable errors in word choice and form ('more better', 'more fast', 'more quiet', 'country develop'), though meaning is generally clear. Range and precision are not sufficient for 6.0.","strengths":[{"quote":"The public transport can carry many people in one time and it is good for enviroment.","comment":"Topical vocabulary such as 'public transport' and 'environment' is used appropriately to convey the main idea."}],"issues":[{"quote":"If the bus is more better, people will use it more and the traffic will be less.","comment":"Double comparative 'more better' is a clear word-formation error.","suggestion":"Use 'better': 'If buses were better, more people would use them and traffic would decrease.'"},{"quote":"So goverment should make it cheap and more fast.","comment":"'More fast' is incorrect and 'cheap' is imprecise here; the spelling 'goverment' is also wrong.","suggestion":"'The government should make fares cheaper and services faster.'"},{"quote":"Both is important for the people and the country develop.","comment":"'Country develop' is an incorrect noun/verb combination and 'Both is' is ungrammatical.","suggestion":"'Both are important for the people and for the country's development.'"}]},"grammar":{"band":5.0,"summary":"A mix of simple and some complex sentences is attempted, but errors are frequent and sometimes impede clarity. Subject-verb agreement, articles, comparatives and verb forms are repeatedly faulty ('goverment should spend', 'many country', 'the city is grow', 'he spend'). Punctuation is basic and sentence boundaries are sometimes unclear, keeping the score at 5.0.","strengths":[{"quote":"If there is no new road the traffic jam will be very bad and people waste a lot of time.","comment":"A conditional structure is attempted and the meaning is clear despite the missing comma."}],"issues":[{"quote":"Nowadays transport is very important problem in many country.","comment":"Missing article and plural form: 'a very important problem in many countries'.","suggestion":"'Nowadays transport is a very important problem in many countries.'"},{"quote":"Because the city is grow and more people buy car every year.","comment":"Incorrect verb form 'is grow' and missing plural 'cars'.","suggestion":"'This is because cities are growing and more people buy cars every year.'"},{"quote":"For example my father drive to work everyday and he spend two hour in the road.","comment":"Third-person singular agreement errors ('drive', 'spend') and 'two hour' should be plural.","suggestion":"'For example, my father drives to work every day and spends two hours on the road.'"}]}},"overall_comment":"这篇作文结构清楚，能回应题目的两个方面并给出平衡立场，但语言准确性和论证深度限制了分数。词汇和语法错误较频繁（如 'more better'、'is grow'、'goverment'），衔接手段机械，例子偏个人化。建议优先修正基础语法与拼写，并练习用因果链扩展论点。","priorities":["修正主谓一致、冠词、比较级和拼写等基础错误（如 'many country'、'more better'、'goverment'）","避免用 'Because' 开头写句子片段，改用从句或连接词整合句子","用因果链或更普遍的例子扩展论点，而不是只给个人经历","减少 'Firstly/Secondly/Also/So' 的机械使用，增加指代和逻辑连接","积累交通与环境话题的常用搭配，替换 'good/bad/important' 等基础词"]}

{"criteria":{"task":{"band":6.5,"summary":"The essay fully addresses all parts of the question, presents a clear position (mostly agree, with a concession for necessary road building), and supports each main idea with explanation and an example. The position is maintained throughout and the conclusion restates it coherently. Development is relevant and adequate, though the supporting ideas are fairly brief and could be extended further for a higher band.","strengths":[{"quote":"I mostly agree with this view, although I believe some road building is still necessary.","comment":"Clear, nuanced position stated in the introduction and sustained to the end."},{"quote":"after my city opened a new metro line, the main road to the city centre became much less crowded during rush hour","comment":"A concrete personal example that effectively supports the efficiency argument."},{"quote":"they should still build roads in places where public transport is not practical","comment":"The concession is developed with a rural/goods rationale and resolved in the conclusion."}],"issues":[{"quote":"Public transport produces less pollution per passenger, so it is a more sustainable option in the long term.","comment":"The environmental paragraph is quite short and relies on general statements without a specific example or data.","suggestion":"Add a brief illustration, e.g. 'For instance, a full bus emits far less CO2 per person than the equivalent number of private cars.'"},{"quote":"poor roads can slow down the economy","comment":"The economic point is asserted but not explained, leaving the concession underdeveloped.","suggestion":"Extend with a short explanation of how efficient freight transport lowers costs for businesses and consumers."}]},"coherence":{"band":6.5,"summary":"The essay is logically organised into a clear introduction, two supporting paragraphs, a concession paragraph and a conclusion, giving good overall progression. Cohesive devices are used appropriately and referencing is generally clear. However, some linkers are fairly conventional and the range of cohesive devices is not especially wide, keeping it below band 7.","strengths":[{"quote":"The main reason to invest in public transport is that","comment":"Signals the paragraph's central idea clearly and aids the reader."},{"quote":"On the other hand, new roads are sometimes needed.","comment":"Effectively marks the shift to the counter-argument, showing balanced structure."}],"issues":[{"quote":"Another advantage is the environment.","comment":"The transition is functional but mechanical; the paragraph topic is introduced with a stock phrase.","suggestion":"Vary the linking, e.g. 'Beyond efficiency, public transport also brings environmental benefits.'"},{"quote":"Also, goods are mostly transported by trucks","comment":"'Also' is a weak connector here and the sentence feels loosely attached to the previous point.","suggestion":"Use a more precise linker such as 'Furthermore' or 'In addition, freight transport relies heavily on trucks.'"}]},"lexical":{"band":6.5,"summary":"The vocabulary is adequate and generally precise, with some good topic-specific collocations such as 'traffic congestion', 'carbon emissions' and 'sustainable option'. There is some attempt at less common lexis, but the range is moderate and repetition of basic items limits the score. Spelling and word formation are accurate throughout.","strengths":[{"quote":"traffic congestion has become a serious problem","comment":"Accurate, natural topic collocation used appropriately."},{"quote":"a more sustainable option in the long term","comment":"Good use of a less common, precise phrase suited to the environmental argument."}],"issues":[{"quote":"many drivers will choose them, which will reduce traffic jams","comment":"'Traffic jams' is informal and repetitive alongside the earlier 'traffic congestion'.","suggestion":"Use a more formal alternative, e.g. 'which will ease congestion' or 'reduce traffic volume'."},{"quote":"poor roads can slow down the economy","comment":"The phrasing is simple and slightly vague; a more precise collocation would raise the band.","suggestion":"Consider 'inadequate roads can hamper economic growth' or 'hinder the efficient movement of goods'."}]},"grammar":{"band":6.5,"summary":"The essay shows a good mix of simple and complex sentences, including conditionals and relative clauses, with a high proportion of error-free sentences. Punctuation is generally accurate. However, the range of complex structures is not especially ambitious and some sentences are fairly basic, keeping it below band 7.","strengths":[{"quote":"If buses and trains are frequent, cheap and reliable, many drivers will choose them","comment":"Accurate first conditional with a well-formed list, showing control of complex structure."},{"quote":"Cars produce a lot of air pollution and carbon emissions, which are harmful to people's health","comment":"Correct non-defining relative clause used naturally."}],"issues":[{"quote":"there are not enough passengers to make train lines profitable, so people depend on cars","comment":"Grammatically correct but a simple compound structure; limited complexity.","suggestion":"Try a more complex form, e.g. 'Since passenger numbers in rural areas are too low to make rail profitable, residents have little choice but to rely on cars.'"},{"quote":"In many cities, traffic congestion has become a serious problem, and governments must decide how to use limited budgets.","comment":"Accurate but a straightforward compound sentence; more varied subordination would help.","suggestion":"Combine ideas with subordination, e.g. 'As traffic congestion worsens in many cities, governments face difficult decisions about how to allocate limited budgets.'"}]}},"overall_comment":"这是一篇结构清晰、立场明确的6.5分作文：四个主体段落分别处理效率、环境、让步与结论，论证相关且有个人例子支撑，语法错误极少。主要提升空间在于论证的深度（环境段和让步段偏简略）、衔接手段的多样性以及词汇的精确度与正式度。若能扩展论据、丰富连接词并提升搭配的正式性，有望稳定达到7.0。","priorities":["扩展环境段与让步段：为每个论点补充具体例子或数据，避免仅停留在概括性陈述。","丰富衔接手段：减少 'Another advantage is...'、'Also' 等程式化连接词，改用更精确的逻辑连接。","提升词汇精确度与正式度：用 'ease congestion'、'hamper economic growth' 等替换口语化或笼统表达。","增加复杂句式的多样性：多用从句、分词结构等，避免过多简单并列句。"]}

{"essay": "How a government allocates its transport budget shapes not only how quickly people travel, but also the kind of cities they live in. Although building new roads whenever traffic worsens has an intuitive appeal, I am convinced that investment should be weighted decisively towards public transport, with road construction reserved for cases where no realistic alternative exists.

The case for new roads rests largely on the assumption that congestion is simply a shortage of capacity. Yet experience from many large cities suggests otherwise: widening a motorway lowers the cost of driving, which in turn draws additional traffic until the new lanes are as clogged as the old ones. This phenomenon, often described as induced demand, means that road building can become an expensive treadmill. Public transport, by contrast, increases the number of people a corridor can carry without a proportional increase in the space consumed, and a single metro line can relieve pressure on an entire network of streets.

Equally important are the distributional consequences. Road spending disproportionately benefits those who own cars, whereas frequent and affordable buses and trains extend opportunity to people who cannot drive or prefer not to. Well-designed transit also allows denser, more walkable neighbourhoods to develop around stations, which reduces the distances people need to travel in the first place, and it cuts emissions at a time when the transport sector remains one of the most stubborn sources of carbon.

That said, a blanket refusal to build any new roads would be misguided. Rural communities and freight logistics depend on reliable highways, and in such contexts targeted upgrades may represent genuine value for money.

On balance, therefore, public transport should receive the lion's share of funding, because it tackles congestion at its root and produces broader social and environmental returns that new roads {"essay": "Online learning has expanded rapidly over the past decade, and some people now argue that it will eventually replace the traditional classroom. In my view, although online courses offer genuine advantages, face-to-face education will remain indispensable.

The most obvious benefit of online learning is flexibility. Students can watch lectures whenever they choose and progress at their own pace, which is particularly valuable for adults who work full-time or care for their families. Online courses can also reach learners in remote areas who would otherwise have no access to qualified teachers. In addition, digital materials can be updated quickly, and learners can replay difficult explanations as often as they need, something that is impossible in a traditional lecture. For many people, these features make online study cheaper and more convenient than attending a college in person.

However, classroom learning provides benefits that are difficult to replicate on a screen. Teachers can notice immediately when a student is confused and adjust their explanations accordingly. Students also develop social skills by working together, discussing ideas and building friendships, and these skills form an important part of education, particularly for children.

Furthermore, many learners find it hard to stay motivated without the structure of a timetable and the presence of classmates. Completion rates for many free online courses are notoriously low, which suggests that a lack of self-discipline is a serious obstacle to online study.

In conclusion, online learning is a valuable supplement that makes education more accessible and flexible, but it is unlikely to replace traditional classrooms, which offer interaction, support and {"essay": "I largely agree that governments should spend more money on improving public transport than on building new roads, although I accept that some road construction remains necessary.

The main reason for prioritising public transport is its efficiency. A single bus or train can carry many people at the same time, so investment in these services reduces traffic jams in big cities far more effectively than adding lanes, which often simply attracts more cars. Public transport is also cheaper for students and old people who do not own a car, so improving it gives these groups better access to work, education and healthcare.

A further argument concerns the environment and public health. Buses and trains produce less pollution per passenger than private cars, so shifting travellers onto public transport would cut air pollution and respiratory illness in crowded urban areas. Spending on new roads, by contrast, tends to encourage more driving and therefore more emissions.

However, new roads are still useful in the countryside, where there are not many buses and residents depend on their cars for long distances. In such areas, a modest amount of road building can connect isolated communities to essential services.

In conclusion, public transport should be the priority for government spending, especially in cities, but some roads are still necessary, particularly in rural regions.",
